text:
incident-bot: PAGER: canary-monitoring alert for service/inference-api (canary pool: canary-q8v2)
incident-bot: symptom=healthcheck_failures; 5xx_rate=6.4% over 3m; latency_p95 up 220ms; abort_criteria=TRUE -> auto-page oncall

sarah: I'm on pager, grabbing context.
sarah: which rollout is this?
raj: that's my canary from the morning — rolled a quantized q8v2 variant to 3% traffic at 09:12 UTC.
raj: I saw a small uptick in error logs in staging but nothing like this.

sarah: ok — canary was up for ~45m. incident-bot says 5xx > abort threshold.
sarah: @deploy-bot can you show canary rollout metadata?
deploy-bot: canary-id=canary-q8v2, started_by=raj, version=2026.07.12-q8v2, target=3%, current=3%, healthchecks=failed(3/5)

maya: throwing my +1 to kill it now if abort criteria met. can we confirm customer impact? any 500s from major routes?
dana: I'm seeing a handful of customer errors in support triage for requests to /v1/generate, most from EU region. So far <10 unique customers but errors spike matches canary timeframe.

leo: quick check of logs (from canary nodes):
```
2026-01-22T09:43:21Z canary-q8v2-1 ERROR handler.go:142 503 upstream-kvcache-miss
2026-01-22T09:44:02Z canary-q8v2-2 ERROR decode.go:88 502 model-inference-fatal: invalid tensor shape
2026-01-22T09:45:12Z canary-q8v2-1 ERROR handler.go:146 503 kvcache-timeout
```

leo: looks like the quantized kernel is throwing decode errors occasionally and causing 5xx cascades.

sarah: meets abort: >5% 5xx and failing healthchecks. I'm going to flip the canary kill-switch now.
sarah: runbook step: toggle feature-flag/kill-switch for canary pool and scale down canary instances, then reroute traffic.

sarah: @raj heads-up, we'll kill the canary and roll back to stable model variant for safety.

sarah: executing kill switch -> `curl -s -X POST "https://ops.redwood.internal/flags/off" -d '{"flag":"canary-q8v2-enabled"}'`
sarah: response: {"ok":true, "flag":"canary-q8v2-enabled","state":"off"}

sarah: scaling canary pool to 0 -> `kubectl -n prod scale deploy canary-q8v2 --replicas=0`
sarah: command returned: scaled

deploy-bot: Canary traffic rebalanced: canary-q8v2 -> 0%, traffic shifted to stable-pool (v2026.06.30).

maya: healthcheck status after kill: p95 latency returning to baseline, 5xx_rate dropping to 0.4% in last 2m.

dana: support: we've sent initial note to affected customers offering ETA/ack and advising to retry; low priority but flagging for monitoring.

raj: apologies team. digging into kernel/shape mismatch. pushing a debug build to qa.

leo: opened temporary short-lived alert suppression for canary alerts and documented the incident in the canary runbook.
sarah: creating incident channel and handing to oncall for postmortem follow-up.
sarah: summary for pager: canary q8v2 triggered abort due to >5% 5xx; kill-switch toggled, scaled down canary, traffic routed back to stable; customer impact small (<10 customers), mitigation completed.

sarah: oncall handoff: @maya taking the lead for follow-up and postmortem. I'll stay available for context.
maya: taking. I'll collect logs, attach the failing model artifacts, and run a replay test to reproduce. planning postmortem checklist now.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-245 - canary-q8v2 abort and rollback. Severity: S2.

sarah: closing pager for this thread — watch for any regressions, keep alerts enabled for stable pool. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — will post the RCA timeline and next steps in #postmortems.

raj: will open PR with additional shape checks and a canary throttling guard to avoid full decode failure cascade.

leo: note for ops: consider updating canary abort criteria to include decoder errors specifically.

sarah: good call. end of thread.
